findings.reason: the honest change is to generalise the existing owner to carry named channel arrays and host the coupling-state family, so member-batch identity lives in one place instead of drifting across two containers that already disagree on the `member()` accessor.
findings.text: `MemberArrayBatch` re-derives the identified-leading-member-axis container (member_ids, unique/non-empty identity validation, stack/unstack, member accessor) that `EnsembleTransportState` in `nova/transport/ensemble.py:52` already owns, landed 2026-08-20 (c792f7d2c, cc542659c) before §2's 2026-08-23 (5c448153a); the same package now carries two member-batch owners with divergent accessors (`member(id)` here, `member(index)` there)

findings.reason: the convergence policy is now authored twice, so any change to tolerance/summary thresholds or the backoff rule lands on the scalar path and silently not on the batch path; the per-member policy should be one shared function both loops call, with the batch loop differing only in its active-mask and refusal accumulation.
findings.text: `solve_window_batch` reimplements the scalar `solve_window` convergence state machine (nova/transport/coupled_window.py:1413-1517): identical `WindowConvergenceReceipt` construction, identical tolerance gate, identical `hard_ceiling_reached / contraction_unavailable / stalled_at_floor / cap_needs_measurement` decision, identical damping backoff and continuation bookkeeping, and it imports the private helpers `_contraction_estimate` and `_window_conservation` across the module boundary (window_batch.py:33-34)

findings.reason: the plan should state the extension-versus-parallel case, and the once-per-exchange invocation it cites as justification is a property of the update callable, not a reason the scalar convergence loop cannot be reused.
findings.text: the plan adds `WindowBatchInput` + `solve_window_batch` as a parallel entry point without saying why `solve_window`'s update contract cannot be widened to take the batched operator signature (`BatchUpdate` differs from `ExchangeSweepResult` only by the batch axis and the once-per-exchange invocation, window_batch.py:369-371); the plan's own published evidence (batch-8 125.2/134.2 vs scalar 158.3/168.6 member-windows/s, ~21% slower) shows the facade buys API shape and identity, not speed

findings.reason: a reuse search that stops at the cross-repo survey is the exact failure mode this rubric exists for; naming the in-repo owners would have changed §2 from "add a batch container family" to "extend the existing one".
findings.text: the plan's reuse map covers the ambix estimator inventory but never cites nova's own prior art: `nova/transport/ensemble.py` (member-batch forward over identified members, 2026-08-20) and `nova/equilibrium/batched_labeller.py` (`BatchedLabeller`, member-axis batching) both already exist in-tree, yet the plan introduces a fresh member-batch vocabulary as if none existed

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — `solve_window_batch` (nova/transport/window_batch.py:374) hides the whole identified-member fixed-point exchange, receipt assembly and fail-closed refusal behind one function and a four-field input record; the interface is smaller than the behaviour it hides.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan forked both the member-batch container family (owner nova/transport/ensemble.py) and the window convergence loop (owner nova/transport/coupled_window.py) rather than extending either.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan's reuse search was the cross-repo ambix survey (scripts/assimilation_seam_survey/report.md) and it did not surface `nova/transport/ensemble.py`, which already owns nova's member-batch machinery and landed three days before §2.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — the batch entry point is a second, parallel entry beside `solve_window` with no stated reason the scalar signature could not be extended to carry the batched update contract.
